tr.darwin dacht dat het leven begon in een:
darwin thought life began in a warm little pond.
his contemporary haeckel saw in the cell no more than a lump of slime.

the egg cell you grew from fits into it five times side by side.
it is the only cell of your body you can see with the naked eye.

tr.elke slag van de pomp: drie natrium erui:
every stroke of the pump: three sodium out, two potassium in, one ATP.
that is how the cell charges itself to seventy millivolts, and keeps it up her whole life.
it costs her a quarter of all her energy. (go ahead, prick a hole: it leaks, and closes by itself.)
tr.bruce lipton noemt dit vlies het brein v: bruce lipton calls this membrane the brain of the cell: here she feels what is outside.
tr.140.000 volt per centimeter over dit vli: 140,000 volts per centimetre across this membrane. air breaks down at 30,000.

tr.stappen van acht nanometer. één ATP per:
steps of eight nanometres. one ATP per step. a hundred steps a second.
the animators left the cell empty, to be able to show this.
in real life she walks through a crowd of billions of proteins, all trembling and colliding.
no one directs the traffic. still everything arrives.
tr.naar ‘the inner life of the cell’ (harva: after ‘the inner life of the cell’ (harvard, 2006), and the sequel that drew the cell full again
tr.laat zien hoe vol het echt is: show how full it really is

tr.(houd ingedrukt: laat de waterstofkernen: (press and hold: let the hydrogen nuclei through)
tr.de cel verbrandt je eten om waterstofker:
the cell burns your food to pump hydrogen nuclei to one side of a membrane.
the only way back is through the mill. it turns, and with every third turn it clamps an ATP shut:
the coin with which everything in the cell is paid.
over a hundred turns a second. every day you make your own weight in ATP this way.
the mitochondrion this stands in was once a free bacterium. it still has its own DNA: from your mother.
tr.in jouw lijf, op dit moment: ongeveer ee: in your body, right now: about a sextillion a second.
tr.ze loopt maar één kant op: wijs vóór haa: she only walks one way: point ahead of her
tr.(beweeg: je trekt de draad uit de kern): (move: you pull the thread out of the nucleus)
tr.twee meter draad in een kern van zes dui:
two metres of thread in a nucleus six thousandths of a millimetre wide:
like stuffing twenty kilometres of the finest yarn into a tennis ball.
drawn as thick as here, the thread from one nucleus would be five thousand kilometres long.
all the thread in your body, laid end to end, reaches to pluto.
tr.drie letters op de draad staan voor één:
three letters on the thread stand for one building block. there are twenty, and each has a letter.
type a word: the cell strings it together, and it folds into a shape that belongs to that word alone.
that is how script becomes a tool: a pump, a mill, a foot.
tr.maar nog geen twee procent van de draad:
but not even two percent of the thread can be read like this. what the rest is for is far from settled.
peter gariaev read the whole thread as language, with homonyms, and as a wave that sends and receives.
that is disputed, and confirmed by no one.
tr.dezelfde twee meter in elke kern: the same two metres in every nucleus
tr.elk streepje een gen. licht: de bladzijd: each stripe a gene. light: the page lies open. a dot: locked.
tr.wat verschilt, is welke bladzijden open:
what differs is which pages lie open: two hundred kinds of cell from one book.
a cell remembers what she is, and passes it on when she divides.
what she lives through opens and closes pages too. what you inherit is not the last word.
tr.rudolf steiner, 1910: het geërfde zit in:
rudolf steiner, 1910: what is inherited sits in the body. the spirit can make up for it.
bruce lipton: it is not the genes that steer the cell, but what she picks up from outside.
tr.een zenuwcel: soms een meter lang, en ne: a nerve cell: sometimes a metre long, and just as old as you
tr.een afweercel: kruipt rond, en onthoudt: an immune cell: crawls around, and remembers a disease for sixty years
tr.een huidcel: plat en taai, en na een maa: a skin cell: flat and tough, and shed again after a month
tr.een rode bloedcel: gooit haar boek weg o: a red blood cell: throws away her book to be able to carry oxygen
tr.een spiercel: vol draden die langs elkaa: a muscle cell: full of threads sliding past each other
tr.een vetcel: één grote druppel voorraad,: a fat cell: one big drop of stores, the nucleus pushed aside
tr.elke levende cel geeft licht. heel weini: every living cell gives off light. very little
tr.fritz-albert popp telde het: enkele tot:
fritz-albert popp counted it: a few to a few hundred particles of light a second,
per square centimetre. a thousand times too weak for your eye. under stress it grows.
(keep still, and your eyes adjust. move wildly, and watch what the sprout does.)
tr.alexander gurwitsch, 1923: een uienworte:
alexander gurwitsch, 1923: one onion root points at another, and there more cells start dividing.
through quartz yes, through glass no. seven hundred papers, then it went quiet. the file was never closed.
(tap the slide between the roots)
tr.popp las er een veld in waarmee cellen e: popp read into it a field with which cells keep each other informed. that is his reading, not a shared one.
tr.van elke honderd moleculen in een cel zi: of every hundred molecules in a cell, ninety-nine are water
tr.gerald pollack: langs een natte wand\nho:
gerald pollack: along a wet wall
water keeps a strip clear of everything.
heat and light make the strip wider.
(shine on it with your hand)
tr.(tik: laat water bevriezen)\nde zeshoek:
(tap: let the water freeze)
the hexagon belongs to the water itself.
no two crystals are alike.
the strip has been measured again by other labs. pollack's explanation, a fourth phase of water, is disputed.
masaru emoto photographed ice crystals after a word or music. he himself called it not science,
but a new art. luc montagnier believed water could keep a signal from DNA:
that has not been independently confirmed. viktor schauberger put it more simply in 1933: water is itself a living being.
tr.het geheel wordt er niet groter van: the whole does not get any bigger
tr.één wordt twee, vier, acht. maar niet in:
one becomes two, four, eight. but not in step: you also see three, five and seven.
only the egg of a sea urchin divides as neatly as in the textbook.
at eight a figure lies over it: the egg of life, drunvalo melchizedek calls it,
the beginning of the flower of life. the figure is a drawing. the real little clump just keeps dividing.
double forty-five times, and there are enough for a whole human.

tr.een cel kan zichzelf opruimen: a cell can clear itself away
tr.als embryo had je peddels. de cellen tus:
as an embryo you had paddles. the cells between your fingers got a sign, and cleared themselves away:
neatly, in little sacs, which the neighbours eat. (stroke between them)
every second almost four million of your cells do the same, and as many new ones arrive.
tr.zo kreeg je vingers: niet aangegroeid, m: that is how you got fingers: not grown on, but carved out.
tr.buren zijn verbonden door poortjes. tik:
neighbours are joined by little gates. tap one, and it runs from cell to cell.
in 2007 a lab at harvard gave every nerve cell of a mouse its own colour:
ninety shades, to tell neighbours apart. brainbow.
what one cell knows, a second later they all know.
tr.de melkweg telt een paar honderd miljard:
the milky way counts a few hundred billion stars. you have a hundred times as many cells.
each dot here stands for fifteen billion of them.
they all came from one point a tenth of a millimetre across.
